links.comparator_used: Same clinicians' initial categorization without AI (sequential paired design, reassessed 1 to 2 weeks later with the AI assessment card)
links.outcome: Reader accuracy of pre-laryngoscopic categorization; sensitivity for precancerous or malignant lesions
links.effect: Accuracy 49.8% before vs 56.8% after AI-assisted review (difference 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI 1.7 to 13.5; P < 0.001); 99 categories changed incorrect to correct vs 43 correct to incorrect (ratio 2.30; 95% CI 1.22 to 5.31); sensitivity for precancerous or malignant lesions 53.9% to 75.0% (difference 21.1 points; 95% CI 4.3 to 42.0)
links.tradeoff: Gains depended on model correctness without clearly selective adoption: accuracy rose 14.7 points when the model was correct and fell 8.7 when incorrect; 43 categories changed from correct to incorrect. The sequential design cannot fully separate AI assistance from reassessment.
links.quote: Across 800 paired assessments, reader accuracy was 49.8% before and 56.8% after review (difference, 7.0 percentage points; 95% CI, 1.7 to 13.5; P < 0.001); 99 categories changed from incorrect to correct and 43 from correct to incorrect (ratio, 2.30; 95% CI, 1.22 to 5.31).

design_hint: clinician review of AI assessment output (human-in-the-loop)
